acceptance_criteria.criterion: isRawModeSupported() returns false when process.stdin.isTTY is falsy
enterRawMode() does not throw in non-TTY environments (graceful no-op or caught error)
restoreTerminal() is safe to call multiple times without side effects
waitForKey() resolves immediately in non-TTY environments
clearScreen() writes the correct ANSI escape sequence
npm run typecheck passes with all terminal modules included

summary: Implemented src/raw-mode.ts with isRawModeSupported(), enterRawMode(), exitRawMode(), and restoreTerminal(). All non-TTY paths are guarded with early returns and/or wrapped in try/catch.
Implemented src/screen.ts with clearScreen() (writes \x1b[2J\x1b[0;0H) and waitForKey() which resolves immediately when !process.stdin.isTTY.
waitForKey() uses process.stdin.once('keypress') and delegates full cleanup to restoreTerminal(), keeping the coordination logic in one place.
npm run typecheck passes with no errors. All 75 existing tests pass (no regressions).

comments.note: readline.emitKeypressEvents(process.stdin) is called both inside enterRawMode() and waitForKey(). Node.js docs state the function is idempotent, so duplicate calls are safe, but if both are called in sequence the redundancy is slightly noisy. A shared guard (track whether events have been enabled) could be added in Phase B if needed.

In waitForKey(), the setRawMode(true) call after the isTTY guard is not wrapped in try/catch (unlike enterRawMode). If isTTY is truthy but setRawMode still throws (unusual, but possible on some CI environments with partial TTY emulation), the promise would reject rather than resolving. Wrapping in try/catch with a resolve() in the catch block would be more defensive. Flagged for Phase B.

exitRawMode() and restoreTerminal() have overlapping behaviour — exitRawMode pauses stdin, restoreTerminal pauses stdin plus removes keypress listeners. The distinction is documented implicitly by name, but a brief JSDoc note clarifying 'use restoreTerminal() after interactive keypress sessions, exitRawMode() for lightweight teardown' would help future contributors.

summary: AC 1–5: Code verified correct by source review. isRawModeSupported() returns false via === true guard (handles undefined). enterRawMode() early-returns on non-TTY. restoreTerminal() uses removeAllListeners + try/catch setRawMode(false) + pause() — all idempotent, safe for repeated calls. waitForKey() resolves immediately when !process.stdin.isTTY. clearScreen() writes \x1b[2J\x1b[0;0H — correct ANSI sequence.
AC 6 (typecheck): PASS — npm run typecheck exits 0 with no errors.

Regression FAIL: npm test --coverage exits code 1. All four coverage thresholds fail (lines 75.22%, functions 74.19%, statements 75.63%, branches 78.94% — all below the 80% minimum). Root cause: vitest.config.ts excludes src/terminal/raw-mode.ts and src/terminal/screen.ts (original plan paths) but WP-004 placed files at src/raw-mode.ts and src/screen.ts. The non-matching exclusion paths leave both new files included in coverage with 0% scores.

The mismatch means both files are included in coverage at 0%, dropping all four thresholds below 80% and causing 'npm test -- --coverage' to exit 1. Fix: change the two exclude entries to 'src/raw-mode.ts' and 'src/screen.ts'.

clearScreen() unconditionally writes ANSI to process.stdout regardless of whether stdout is a TTY. In piped or CI environments this produces garbage ANSI bytes in captured output. No explicit AC covers this, but a !process.stdout.isTTY guard would be the defensive choice. Flagged for Phase B consideration.

In waitForKey(), process.stdin.setRawMode(true) is called after the !isTTY guard but is not wrapped in try/catch (unlike the equivalent path in enterRawMode()). On environments where isTTY is truthy but setRawMode still throws (e.g., partial TTY emulation), the returned Promise would reject instead of resolving. This was also flagged by the Developer — confirming it remains unaddressed.

DRY observation recorded: waitForKey() manually re-implements the three-line enterRawMode() body. No behavioral bug, but creates a future divergence risk if enterRawMode() is updated without updating waitForKey().

comments.note: Fix-Forward: Expanded JSDoc on exitRawMode() in src/raw-mode.ts to document the usage distinction from restoreTerminal(). Added: 'Use exitRawMode() for lightweight teardown when no keypress listeners were registered. For full cleanup after an interactive keypress session, prefer restoreTerminal() which also removes keypress event listeners.' Pure documentation addition — zero behavioral change. Addresses Developer's own observation from the implementation pipeline.

DRY violation in waitForKey() (src/screen.ts lines 36-39): the three-line sequence `readline.emitKeypressEvents(process.stdin); process.stdin.setRawMode(true); process.stdin.resume();` duplicates the core body of enterRawMode(). If enterRawMode() is updated in Phase B (e.g., with better error handling), waitForKey() will not inherit the fix automatically. Recommend replacing those 3 lines with a call to enterRawMode() in Phase B — this would simultaneously eliminate the duplication and add the missing try/catch protection.

Phase B hardening reminder (confirmed by Developer + QA): (1) process.stdin.setRawMode(true) in waitForKey() is not wrapped in try/catch — on partial-TTY environments where isTTY is truthy but setRawMode throws, the returned Promise rejects instead of resolving. (2) clearScreen() writes ANSI bytes unconditionally regardless of process.stdout.isTTY — produces garbage in piped/CI output capturing. Both are explicitly Phase B scope.
